pull_request.title: Share opt-in heap memory call observations for tests
pull_request.body:
Metrics maintains a write-counting Memory wrapper while Memory's allocation example and unit tests share a private copy of the same observation pattern. This contribution exports the existing observer through an opt-in `test-support` feature and removes the example-owned implementation.

`test_support::{Counts, Metered}` uses Memory's exact exported `Memory`/`VectorMemory` types. Clones share storage and counters; reset clears only observations. Read/write calls are observed before delegation, growth after return, and successful growth contributes pages. Numeric counts clip with a sticky actual-overflow flag. Direct backend access bypasses observation. These are heap-memory test effects, never IC instructions, cycles or timing evidence.

Internal allocation tests and the existing example use the shared owner. The example requires `--features test-support` and refuses overflowed observations before reporting. No timing driver was added or executed. Native validation includes a focused observer gate, and native compiler-floor CI compiles the feature. The feature remains off for ordinary library builds; no dependencies, package versions, locks or stored data change.

Validation: both observer boundary tests and all 11 affected allocation unit tests pass; strict native/Wasm Clippy, example compilation, feature Rustdoc, format checks and Rust 1.88 native/Wasm library checks plus native all-targets pass. Workflow lint and changed-document links pass. No full local validation, runtime/IC performance or hosted macOS acceptance is claimed. Initial formatting/Clippy failures remain in local logs; the corrected checks pass.

This isolated contribution starts from released 0.38.0 (`4118e41`) and leaves the normal sibling checkout's bounded-writer work untouched. Metrics must retain its local observer until a release containing the new feature is published; it will then select the registry feature as a development dependency and remove its duplicate.

## Latest adoption review — 2026-10-20

The official sparse-index endpoint `https://index.crates.io/ic/-t/ic-testkit-native` returns HTTP 404. Testkit PR #97 remains open and unmerged at `4c4c66b3dcfcba521dd36db73580c34cd12db599`. The available Testkit main checkout at `96c0124` has no supplying package or observer API. There is still no published replacement to qualify.

Metrics' reviewed base is release source `e972af583cb9e6e669bbe0b46f6ab398cc08a7d9` (0.14.9), plus an incoming Memory 0.49.2 lock update with Storage 0.5.8. All 22 stable units, three doctests, strict native/Wasm stable Clippy, native all-target/Wasm library Rust 1.91 checks and production dependency admission pass locally on that graph. These are producer checks, not observer adoption, publication, full CI or macOS acceptance.

Keep `WriteCountingMemory` in `crates/ic-metrics-stable/src/tests.rs` until a compatible published owner exists. No path override, new observation engine or development dependency is introduced. Earlier source-bound receipts remain in this issue's history.

## Adoption acceptance

- Review the published `ic-testkit-native::memory::{MeteredMemory, MemoryIoCounts}` API and its opt-in `stable-memory` feature, including sticky actual-overflow/report-refusal behavior.
- Select it through the root catalog and a stable-package development dependency only. Qualify the exact backing-trait identity shared by Memory/Storage; retain governed Storage access and the dependency-free arithmetic graph. No Host/PocketIC dependency may enter either production graph.
- Preserve shared backing/counter clone behavior, reset without clearing stored bytes, growth/refusal and specialized unsafe-read behavior. Keep no-write, malformed-record and regression assertions. Remove the local observer completely only after the replacement passes.
- Run named stable tests, native/Wasm lint and the advertised compiler-floor checks on the selected graph. Native IO call counts are behavior evidence, not IC instruction/cycle measurements.

This issue remains open for publication and consumer adoption; the local Memory/Storage patch qualification does not complete it.

issue.body:
Reconcile bounded fixture admission from this PR and typed setup/memory transfer from #116 against released Memory 0.44.0. Refs #104; supersedes #116 once this refreshed contribution is available for review.

`test-support` adds typed setup/write refusal, explicit bounded fresh/retained entry points and admitted-memory transfer. Retained headers, capacity and selected byte limits are checked before Cell loads its payload; invalid retained bytes are never initialized as fresh. Existing `new`/`set` keep their panic convention. The temporary runtime is dropped after authority verification and opening, retaining only the cell/handle and its ceiling. Codecs, initialization and lifecycle remain caller-owned. Bootstrap can advance allocation-ledger metadata before later Cell refusal; backing IO and publication can still panic.

The one header-admission helper serves both fixtures and the unchanged bounded ledger reader. There is no dependency or stored-format change. Pending notes select compatible 0.44.1 without changing package versions or lockfiles.

Validation on the reconciled source: 197 library tests pass (six explicit allocation measurements remain ignored); all eight fixture tests pass, including retained-header preservation, header-only oversized refusal, bounded writes, short replacement and missing Cell admission. Strict feature Clippy, warning-denied feature Rustdoc, formatting, Rust 1.91 native/all-target and Wasm checks, and current-toolchain feature Wasm compilation pass. All five default-feature raw Wasm probes have no size increase: core −97 bytes, diagnostics unchanged in size, admission −105, runtime integration −91 and installed IO −91.

Full release validation, installed qualification of this new head and native macOS acceptance were not run locally. Required hosted checks remain separate. Blob, Jobs and Auth adoption still requires this extension to be integrated/published and qualified by those consumers; their earlier-source evidence is not current adoption.

issue.title: Share explicit fixture byte-cell construction for Blob probes

repository.name: ic-memory
repository.description: Durable stable-memory allocation governance for Internet Computer canisters

issue.body:
## Delivered producer — Memory 0.45.0

The bounded/fallible FixtureCell extension from PR #105 and the superseded #116 is delivered in Memory 0.45.0. The current API provides typed setup/write refusal, explicit bounded fresh/retained entry points and admitted-memory transfer. Header, capacity and byte limits are admitted before payload loading; missing/corrupt retained cells are not initialized as fresh. Writes refuse oversize values before mutation. The fixture keeps its Cell/handle and ceiling after the temporary bootstrap runtime is dropped. The redundant authority recheck from the earlier PR is removed under the current successful-bootstrap contract.

Codecs, initialization, retained-data disposition and lifecycle remain consumer-owned. Bootstrap may update ledger metadata before a later Cell refusal; substrate IO/publication may panic. Jobs #50 and the linked Blob/Auth adoption remain separate consumer work. Their older-source evidence does not establish current adoption.

## Accepted delivery

Released Memory **0.45.0**, `93463259a07295f50146beb57c36adab303d9a37`, retains this implementation and its owning regression checks. The [complete current CI matrix](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-memory/actions/runs/38931395729) passes tooling lint and all three full-test, MSRV and installed-runtime lanes (Ubuntu, macOS ARM and macOS Intel). The full-test gate includes release-helper/adapters and explicit fixture-cell feature qualification; MSRV checks all targets with `test-support`. The selected snapshot is Shared Tooling 0.15.0, `3bef3f2daec7f64f875397ed4d53d5b9e2e68a08`. Earlier failed/cancelled runs remain historical evidence. This completes this issue’s producer/adoption acceptance; it does not claim downstream application adoption.

+bytes and counters; reset changes only the observation window. Counters clip with
+a sticky actual-overflow flag; empty operations remain observable calls. Direct
+backend access bypasses observation. These are heap-memory calls rather than IC
